note: X is badly garbled and misreads the leaf (e.g. 'rex signa orit[ur]' for 'sex signa oriuntur', '20000' for '252000', 'Duo aute[m] circuli' for 'Horum autem circulorum'), whereas Y follows the hand closely.
Y matches the print with 'quorunque' and 'quoniam et in ea legitur'; X has 'quorumque' and drops the 'et'.
X misreads 'inania utilibus' as 'immania', a change of sense, and also has 'aspernerentur' and 'nobiliaribus' where the print reads 'aspernarentur' and 'nobilioribus'.
The body text is identical apart from long-s use; the only other difference is the header ('Oraculis.' vs the printed 'Oraculu.').
X drops the line 'So war ein Christ gebilt nach CHRISTI Wort und Leben/' and garbles the next one as 'So saher Christlich aus'.
X correctly reads 'relicturo' and the Greek 'ἄρθρα σὺν ἄρθροις', where Y has 'relicto' and 'ἄνδρα σὺν ἀνδρείοις'; X's only slip is 'εὐνούχισαν' for the printed 'εὐνουχίσθησαν'.
X keeps the printed 'angenohmen' and 'Dispositon' and gets the dashes right ('— —, —, und —'); Y normalises the spelling and adds an extra dash plus a superscript 'a'.
X garbles many entries (e.g. 'Balatus.us.ui.o damo ꝓui' for 'dicitur clamor ouium') and leaves out the printed 'a balea baleos vel balerica vel balearis'; Y expands the abbreviations faithfully.
The texts are nearly identical, but X misreads 'weitläuftiger' as 'weitläufriger'; the other differences are only in how the brace layout is rendered.

Y drops words from the Latin ('verba o-' becomes 'verationemque', 'qui solem ipsum' becomes 'quibus ipsum'), misreads 'eum concentum' as 'cum concentu', and garbles more of the Greek (e.g. 'δὲ' for 'γὰρ').
